abstract: The October 21, 2026 monthly refresh of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab's Canaries Dashboard, built with ADP Research on a five-year balanced sample of firms using ADP payroll services and workers matched to an occupation code. Data vintage 2026-10-16, observations through September 2026. Early-career workers aged 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations are contracting at 3.4% per year since ChatGPT's release, against 2.1% annual growth in the least-exposed occupations; over the past year the most-exposed group contracted 3.7% while the least-exposed grew 0.2%. Across all ages, the most-exposed occupations are growing 1.0% per year against 2.1% for the least exposed, but contracted 0.5% year over year. The early-career employment index for the most-exposed quintile stood at 87.66 in September 2026 (November 2022 = 100), against 108.4 for the least-exposed quintile. The dashboard's headline remains the August 2026 paper's 19% kept-pace shortfall for ages 22-25 (June 2026 data); this release adds months but no new relative estimate.
keyFindings: Ages 22-25, most AI-exposed occupations: contracting at 3.4% per year since November 2022, versus 2.1% per year growth in the least exposed
Ages 22-25, year over year to September 2026: most-exposed occupations contracted 3.7%, least-exposed grew 0.2%
All ages: most-exposed occupations growing 1.0% per year since ChatGPT versus 2.1% for the least exposed; most-exposed contracted 0.5% year over year
All occupations: early-career (22-25) employment contracting 0.8% per year; developing workers (31-34) growing 0.7% and mid-career (35-40) growing 2.9% per year
Ages 22-25 employment index, September 2026 (Nov 2022 = 100): Q1 least exposed 108.4, Q2 110.1, Q3 106.7, Q4 92.33, Q5 most exposed 87.66
Versus the September 23 release (August data): early-career most-exposed annualized contraction eased from 3.6% to 3.4% per year; all-ages most-exposed YoY moved from -0.6% to -0.5%
methodology: Balanced sample of firms with five years of ADP payroll history, rolled forward one month each release; restricted to workers matched to an occupation code. At launch (five years ending April 2026) the sample comprised 25,000 firms and 4.6 million workers in November 2022 across 730+ occupations. Occupations are grouped into quintiles of the Eloundou et al. (2024) GPT-4 exposure measure, weighting occupations equally rather than by employment. Employment indexes are normalized to November 2022 = 100; annualized growth and year-over-year change are computed upstream from the indexes and published as downloadable CSVs with data dictionaries.
qualifiers: Tier 1 - administrative payroll data from a Stanford DEL and ADP Research collaboration, not peer-reviewed. DEL states the dashboard 'measures the correlation between occupational exposure measures and employment trends in our sample, rather than a causal link', and that the sample 'represents neither the entire U.S. labor market nor the universe of firms using ADP payroll services'. The balanced-panel restriction shuts down firm entry and exit and reallocation to firms outside ADP. Because the five-year window rolls forward monthly, each release restates earlier months: index levels from different releases are not one continuous series. The dashboard publishes index levels and per-quintile growth rates, not a relative shortfall; the 19% kept-pace gap is the August 2026 paper's estimate on June 2026 data and has not been updated.
